```{r}
safe_sum <- function(x) if (anyNA(x)) NA_real_ else sum(x)
format_count <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "Suppressed", scales::comma(x))
read_result <- function(file) {
  path <- file.path(results_dir, file)
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
}

cohort_flow <- read_result("cohort_flow.csv")
complete_flow <- read_result("complete_case_flow.csv")
transfer_flow <- read_result("transfer_exclusions.csv")
table1 <- read_result("table1.csv")
crude <- read_result("crude_weighted_risks.csv")
adjusted_risks <- read_result("model_adjusted_risks.csv")
adjusted_contrasts <- read_result("model_adjusted_contrasts.csv")
model_coefficients <- read_result("model_coefficients.csv")
sensitivity <- read_result("sensitivity_results.csv")
sensitivity_risks <- read_result("sensitivity_adjusted_risks.csv")
sensitivity_contrasts <- read_result("sensitivity_adjusted_contrasts.csv")

mortality <- read_result("first_readmission_mortality.csv")

model_rows <- function(data, preferred = "primary_enriched") {
  if (is.null(data) || !nrow(data)) return(NULL)
  if ("model" %in% names(data)) {
    chosen <- data |> filter(.data$model == preferred)
    if (nrow(chosen)) return(chosen)
    return(data[0, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  data[0, , drop = FALSE]
}

model_fit_summary_row <- function(data, model_label) {
  data |>
    filter(.data$model == .env$model_label, !is.na(.data$term)) |>
    slice(1)
}

primary_label <- function(data) {
  if (is.null(data) || !"model" %in% names(data) || !nrow(data)) return("unavailable")
  unique(data$model)[1]
}
risks_primary <- model_rows(adjusted_risks)
contrasts_primary <- model_rows(adjusted_contrasts)
summary_primary <- if (!is.null(analysis_summary) && "model" %in% names(analysis_summary)) {
  analysis_summary |> filter(.data$model == "primary_enriched")
} else NULL
coefficients_primary <- model_rows(model_coefficients)
primary_groups_present <- !is.null(risks_primary) && all(c("same", "different") %in% as.character(risks_primary$group))
primary_contrast_present <- !is.null(contrasts_primary) &&
  "different_vs_same" %in% as.character(contrasts_primary$contrast)
primary_available <- identical(primary_label(risks_primary), "primary_enriched") &&
  identical(primary_label(contrasts_primary), "primary_enriched") &&
  !is.null(summary_primary) && nrow(summary_primary) == 1L &&
  identical(primary_label(coefficients_primary), "primary_enriched") &&
  primary_groups_present && primary_contrast_present
if (!primary_available) {
  stop("Certified primary_enriched risks, contrast, coefficients, and analysis summary are required.")
}
format_n <- function(x) if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) "not available" else format(round(x), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
format_knot_values <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return("not available")
  values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(strsplit(as.character(x), ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
  if (anyNA(values)) return(as.character(x))
  paste(sprintf("%.2f", values), collapse = "; ")
}
format_pct <- function(x, digits = 1) if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) "not available" else sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * x)
format_pp <- function(x, digits = 2) if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) "not available" else sprintf(paste0("%+.", digits, "f percentage points"), 100 * x)
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, scale = c("pct", "pp", "number"), digits = 2) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  if (any(lengths(list(est, lo, hi)) == 0) || anyNA(c(est, lo, hi))) return("not available")
  mult <- if (scale %in% c("pct", "pp")) 100 else 1
  if (scale == "pct") {
    return(sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%% (95%% CI %.", digits, "f%% to %.", digits, "f%%)"), mult * est, mult * lo, mult * hi))
  }
  if (scale == "pp") {
    return(sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f percentage points (95%% CI %.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"), mult * est, mult * lo, mult * hi))
  }
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (95%% CI %.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"), est, lo, hi)
}
format_ci_rows <- function(est, lo, hi, scale = "number", digits = 2) {
  vapply(seq_along(est), function(i) fmt_ci(est[[i]], lo[[i]], hi[[i]], scale, digits), character(1))
}

label_table1 <- function(variable, level) {
  variable <- as.character(variable)
  level <- as.character(level)
  label <- unname(variable_labels[variable])
  label[is.na(label)] <- variable[is.na(label)]
  level_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    variable == "FEMALE" & level == "0" ~ "No",
    variable == "FEMALE" & level == "1" ~ "Yes",
    grepl("^index_ynel[0-9]+$", variable) & level == "0" ~ "Absent",
    grepl("^index_ynel[0-9]+$", variable) & level == "1" ~ "Present",
    variable == "index_APRDRG_SEVERITY" & level == "0" ~ "No class specified",
    variable == "index_APRDRG_SEVERITY" & level == "1" ~ "Minor",
    variable == "index_APRDRG_SEVERITY" & level == "2" ~ "Moderate",
    variable == "index_APRDRG_SEVERITY" & level == "3" ~ "Major",
    variable == "index_APRDRG_SEVERITY" & level == "4" ~ "Extreme",
    variable == "index_DISPUNIFORM" & level == "1" ~ "Routine discharge home",
    variable == "index_DISPUNIFORM" & level == "5" ~ "Other facility transfer",
    variable == "index_DISPUNIFORM" & level == "6" ~ "Home health care",
    variable == "index_DISPUNIFORM" & level == "7" ~ "Against medical advice",
    variable == "HOSP_BEDSIZE" & level == "1" ~ "Small",
    variable == "HOSP_BEDSIZE" & level == "2" ~ "Medium",
    variable == "HOSP_BEDSIZE" & level == "3" ~ "Large",
    variable == "HOSP_UR_TEACH" & level == "0" ~ "Metropolitan non-teaching",
    variable == "HOSP_UR_TEACH" & level == "1" ~ "Metropolitan teaching",
    variable == "HOSP_UR_TEACH" & level == "2" ~ "Non-metropolitan hospital",
    variable == "H_CONTRL" & level == "1" ~ "Government, nonfederal",
    variable == "H_CONTRL" & level == "2" ~ "Private, not-for-profit",
    variable == "H_CONTRL" & level == "3" ~ "Private investor-owned",
    variable == "PAY1" & level == "1" ~ "Medicare",
    variable == "PAY1" & level == "2" ~ "Medicaid",
    variable == "PAY1" & level == "3" ~ "Private insurance",
    variable == "PAY1" & level == "4" ~ "Self-pay",
    variable == "PAY1" & level == "5" ~ "No charge",
    variable == "PAY1" & level == "6" ~ "Other payer",
    variable == "ZIPINC_QRTL" ~ paste("Income quartile", level),
    variable == "PL_NCHS" & level == "1" ~ "Central county, metro 1 million or more",
    variable == "PL_NCHS" & level == "2" ~ "Fringe county, metro 1 million or more",
    variable == "PL_NCHS" & level == "3" ~ "County, metro 250,000 to 999,999",
    variable == "PL_NCHS" & level == "4" ~ "County, metro 50,000 to 249,999",
    variable == "PL_NCHS" & level == "5" ~ "Micropolitan",
    variable == "PL_NCHS" & level == "6" ~ "Nonmetropolitan, nonmicropolitan",
    TRUE ~ level
  )
  tibble::tibble(Variable = label, Category = level_label)
}
format_risk_ci <- function(est, lo, hi) {
  out <- rep("Suppressed or unavailable", length(est))
  ok <- !is.na(est) & !is.na(lo) & !is.na(hi)
  out[ok] <- sprintf("%.2f%% (%.2f to %.2f)", 100 * est[ok], 100 * lo[ok], 100 * hi[ok])
  out
}
get_row <- function(data, column, values) {
  if (is.null(data)) return(NULL)
  out <- data |> filter(.data[[column]] %in% values)
  if (!nrow(out)) NULL else out[1, , drop = FALSE]
}
is_same_group <- function(x) as.character(x) %in% c("same", "same_hospital")
is_different_group <- function(x) as.character(x) %in% c("different", "different_hospital")
is_risk_difference <- function(x) grepl("(^rd$|risk.?difference)", tolower(as.character(x)))
get_risk_difference <- function(data) {
  if (is.null(data)) return(NULL)
  if ("contrast" %in% names(data)) {
    out <- data |> filter(.data$contrast == "different_vs_same")
    return(if (!nrow(out)) NULL else out[1, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  if (!"measure" %in% names(data)) return(NULL)
  out <- data |> filter(is_risk_difference(.data$measure))
  if (!nrow(out)) NULL else out[1, , drop = FALSE]
}
display_group <- function(x) dplyr::case_when(
  is_same_group(x) ~ "Same hospital",
  is_different_group(x) ~ "Different hospital",
  TRUE ~ as.character(x)
)
safe_kable <- function(data, caption = NULL, digits = 2) {
  if (is.null(data) || !nrow(data)) return(knitr::asis_output("_Not available in the current certified aggregate outputs._"))
  knitr::kable(data, caption = caption, digits = digits, booktabs = TRUE)
}
word_flex_table <- function(data, caption, widths, font_size = 9, split_rows = TRUE) {
  if (!word_output) stop("Fixed-width Word tables are only available in the DOCX format.")
  if (length(widths) != ncol(data) || is.null(names(widths)) || !identical(names(widths), names(data))) {
    stop("Word table widths must be named in the same order as the displayed columns.")
  }
  table <- flextable::flextable(data)
  table <- flextable::set_table_properties(table, layout = "fixed", width = 1,
    opts_word = list(split = split_rows, repeat_headers = TRUE))
  table <- flextable::width(table, j = names(widths), width = as.numeric(widths))
  table <- flextable::font(table, fontname = "Arial", part = "all")
  table <- flextable::fontsize(table, size = font_size, part = "all")
  table <- flextable::bold(table, part = "header")
  table <- flextable::valign(table, valign = "top", part = "all")
  table <- flextable::align(table, j = names(widths)[[1]], align = "left", part = "all")
  table <- flextable::align(table, j = names(widths)[-1], align = "center", part = "all")
  flextable::set_caption(table, caption = caption)
}
```

## Structured abstract

### Background

Hospital switching at a readmission can reflect care transitions, referral, access, patient preference, and clinical routing. The association between switching at a first readmission and a further admission after discharge from that readmission is not necessarily a measure of fragmented care or hospital quality.

### Objectives

To estimate the association between a different versus same hospital for the first all-cause readmission after an eligible heart-failure (HF) index hospitalization and a second readmission, defined as any inpatient admission within 30 days after the first-readmission discharge.

### Methods

This retrospective cohort study uses the 2016–2022 HCUP Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD). Adults with an eligible principal-diagnosis HF hospitalization in January through October were followed to a first **all-cause** readmission within 30 days; HF diagnosis at that first readmission was not required for cohort entry. The analytic population is further restricted to people recorded as alive at discharge from that readmission. The outcome, termed the second readmission, is any inpatient admission within 30 days after the first-readmission discharge. The target is the survey-weighted conditional association among people reaching this survivor cohort. The analysis plan was revised retrospectively before the new outcome models were fit; it was not prespecified before the study.

```{r}
#| label: abstract-model
#| results: asis
if (primary_available) {
  cat("Among people in the survivor cohort after an all-cause first readmission, the primary analysis used a survey-weighted logistic model with year, sex, payer, ZIP income quartile, county rurality, index-hospital bed size, urban-teaching status and ownership, natural splines for age and log(1 + index length of stay), index discharge disposition, APR-DRG severity, and mapped legacy Elixhauser indicators that were nonconstant and estimable. Standardized risks were estimated with predictive margins. The fitted formula, outcome-blind spline knots, and any structural simplifications are reported in the supplement.")
}
```

### Results

```{r}
#| label: abstract-results
#| results: asis
if (primary_available) {
  same <- get_row(risks_primary, "group", c("same", "same_hospital"))
  diff <- get_row(risks_primary, "group", c("different", "different_hospital"))
  rd <- get_risk_difference(contrasts_primary)
  n_primary <- summary_primary$n[1]
  cat("The revised primary model included ", format_n(n_primary),
      " complete cases. The adjusted risk was ",
      fmt_ci(same$risk, same$ci_low, same$ci_high, "pct", 2),
      " after a same-hospital first readmission (n = ", format_n(same$n), "), and ",
      fmt_ci(diff$risk, diff$ci_low, diff$ci_high, "pct", 2),
      " after a different-hospital first readmission (n = ", format_n(diff$n), "). The adjusted risk difference (different minus same hospital) was ",
      fmt_ci(rd$risk_difference, rd$rd_ci_low, rd$rd_ci_high, "pp", 2), ".", sep = "")
}
```

### Conclusions

The analysis concerns a selected group who had a first readmission and survived to its discharge. The observed association cannot establish that changing hospitals causes or prevents another admission. NRD does not capture out-of-hospital deaths or readmissions across states or calendar-year boundaries.

## Introduction

Heart-failure readmissions are common markers of illness burden and care transitions. A readmission to a hospital different from the index hospital may result from patient choice, referral, emergency routing, geography, insurance networks, capacity, or clinical need. The hospital identifier therefore describes site continuity in the discharge data; it does not reveal whether clinicians shared records, whether a transfer was clinically appropriate, or whether care was fragmented.

Prior observational work has compared outcomes during same- versus different-hospital HF readmissions in Canadian and U.S. cohorts ([McAlister et al](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5524066/); [Lahewala et al](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30579719/)). VA research has examined later readmissions after cross-system use ([Axon et al](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26995383/)), and repeat HF admissions have been described in NRD ([Thandra et al](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36152813/)). A systematic review identified a small set of studies addressing later or third admissions, with populations and exposure definitions that differ from the present question ([Snow et al](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7210367/)). More recent NRD work continues to study same- versus different-hospital readmission outcomes ([Turbow et al](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11090805/); [Verma et al](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38938260/)). These studies motivate examining what happens after the first readmission, while leaving important differences in populations, exposure definitions, and follow-up. We therefore avoid a novelty claim and frame the question narrowly: among adults with an eligible HF index admission who are readmitted within 30 days and discharged alive from that first readmission, is a different-hospital first readmission associated with another inpatient admission within the following 30 days?

## Methods

### Design and data source

We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of the HCUP NRD for 2016–2022. The NRD is a state-based, all-payer inpatient database designed to support within-year linkage of hospital discharges in participating states. Its discharge weights support inference to the NRD target universe for each annual sample, not to every U.S. patient or to longitudinal care across years and states. Patient linkage identifiers, hospital identifiers, and sampling strata are year-specific; admissions after a year boundary and admissions in another state are not linked in this analysis.

### Cohort construction

Within each year, we selected adults aged 18 years or older with a principal diagnosis matching the project’s administrative HF phenotype and an index discharge from January through October. The phenotype uses normalized ICD-10-CM principal-diagnosis prefixes `I50`, `I110`, `I130`, `I132`, or `I0981`. For each patient-year, the earliest eligible index admission is selected using the source ordering by `NRD_DAYSTOEVENT` and `KEY_NRD`. Index discharges with recorded in-hospital death, unavailable linkage or hospital identifiers, or the documented same-day event and transfer restrictions are excluded according to the cohort code.

The cohort flow is ordered by event time. We identify the first all-cause readmission within 30 days after the index discharge before applying the first-readmission discharge-status and follow-up restrictions. To enter the second-stage cohort, the first readmission must be discharged alive (`DIED=0`), occur early enough to allow 30 days of within-year follow-up, and meet the same-day, rehabilitation-transfer, and acute-transfer disposition rules implemented in the code. The report uses the published coarsened transfer flow and does not reveal private component counts.

### Exposure Outcome and Estimand

The exposure is a different-hospital first readmission: the `HOSP_NRD` identifier for the first readmission differs from that of the HF index admission. The comparator is a first readmission at the same hospital identifier. This operational measure captures hospital-site switching within a year; it does not directly measure provider continuity, shared records, or a health-system relationship.

Follow-up for the primary outcome begins at discharge from the first readmission. The second readmission is any inpatient admission within 30 days. It is not restricted to HF and is not labeled unplanned. Patients are censored by the available within-year follow-up boundary; the data do not identify out-of-hospital death as a competing event.

The estimand is the survey-weighted, covariate-adjusted difference in predicted 30-day admission risks among adults who experienced the eligible index HF hospitalization, had a first all-cause readmission within 30 days, and were recorded alive at discharge from that first readmission. Conditioning on both readmission and survival defines a selected survivor population and may induce selection bias. This is an adjusted association, not a causal effect of hospital switching.

### Covariates and statistical analysis

The revised primary model included year, sex, payer, ZIP income quartile, county urban-rural category, index-hospital bed size, index-hospital urban-teaching status and ownership, natural cubic splines for age and log(1 + index length of stay), index discharge disposition, APR-DRG severity category, and all mapped legacy Elixhauser indicators that were nonconstant and estimable. APR-DRG severity code 0 was retained as a category distinct from missingness; no Elixhauser summary count was included with the individual indicators. Spline knots were set at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles in the primary complete-case population without using the outcome. The final fitted formula, computed knot locations, and any structurally dropped terms are reported from the analysis summary. All adjustment variables refer to the index admission before the first-readmission destination, although claims-based severity and comorbidity flags may include conditions recorded during that stay. A matched historical-specification refit on the revised primary complete-case population is provided as a model comparison.

Table 1 categories follow the HCUP NRD definitions for [uniform discharge disposition](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/dispuniform/nrdnote.jsp), [hospital teaching status](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/hosp_ur_teach/nrdnote.jsp), [hospital ownership](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/h_contrl/nrdnote.jsp), [hospital bed size](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/hosp_bedsize/nrdnote.jsp), [expected primary payer](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/pay1/nrdnote.jsp), and [NCHS county urban–rural categories](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/pl_nchs/nrdnote.jsp). In particular, HOSP_UR_TEACH codes 0, 1, and 2 mean metropolitan non-teaching, metropolitan teaching, and non-metropolitan hospital, respectively.

This model revision was made retrospectively before refitting outcome models and is not a pre-study prespecified analysis. Structural changes for empty or aliased terms, if any, followed the documented rules and did not use outcome significance or direction.

**HF index admission and discharge.** Demographics, hospital characteristics, year, index length of stay, discharge disposition, APR-DRG severity (including unclassified status), and individual legacy Elixhauser indicators precede the first-readmission destination. The revised primary model uses index-admission covariates with flexible age and index-length-of-stay terms. Claims-based severity and comorbidity flags can include conditions recorded during the index stay.

**Interval before first readmission.** Days from index discharge to first readmission occur before the readmission destination is known. Where included, this timing is distinguished from characteristics recorded during the first readmission.

**First readmission.** Diagnosis, severity, elective-status flags, hospital characteristics, and length of stay are concurrent with or follow destination selection. They are excluded from primary adjustment and considered separately only in supported sensitivity or secondary specifications.

**After first-readmission discharge.** The second readmission and its length of stay are post-exposure outcomes, not baseline confounders.

We use the annual NRD discharge weight, hospital as the primary sampling unit, and the year-specific NRD stratum. Year-specific identifiers are retained when pooling annual files. Survey-weighted logistic regression and design-based standardized predictive margins estimate the adjusted group risks and contrasts. The main effect measure is the risk difference (different minus same hospital), reported in percentage points with a 95% confidence interval. The risk ratio is secondary. Coefficients are reported on the scale used by the analysis output and are not interpreted as risk ratios. The supplement gives model convergence and rank, survey design degrees of freedom, fitted formula, spline knots, and alternate specifications.

The primary analysis is complete-case for model covariates. We report the analytic flow and covariate missingness by year and exposure group. No missing-category model was fitted. Complete-case analyses can be biased if covariate missingness is informative. The analysis plan and reporting checklist distinguish planned revision checks from post hoc decisions; this retrospective revision is not described as preregistered.

### Ethics Funding and Author Information

**Author confirmation required before submission:** institutional review board determination and any waiver or exemption; applicable HCUP data-use compliance statement; author affiliations and contributions; funding and funder role; acknowledgments; and conflicts of interest. These details are intentionally not inferred from the analysis files.

## Results

### Cohort and analysis population

```{r}
#| label: flow-summary
if (!is.null(cohort_flow)) {
  flow_summary <- cohort_flow |>
    summarise(
      years = paste(range(YEAR, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "–"),
      eligible_n = safe_sum(eligible_first_index_n),
      first_readmitted_n = safe_sum(first_readmitted_30d_n),
      second_stage_n = safe_sum(second_stage_eligible_n),
      eligible_weighted = safe_sum(eligible_first_index_weighted),
      first_readmitted_weighted = safe_sum(first_readmitted_30d_weighted),
      second_stage_weighted = safe_sum(second_stage_eligible_weighted)
    ) |>
    mutate(across(ends_with("weighted"), ~ round(.x))) |>
    mutate(across(-years, format_count)) |>
    rename(`Unweighted count` = eligible_n, `NRD-weighted estimate` = eligible_weighted)
  if (word_output) {
    flow_summary_display <- tibble::tibble(
      Stage = c("Eligible HF index admissions", "First all-cause readmission within 30 days", "Alive survivor cohort after first readmission"),
      `Unweighted n` = c(flow_summary$`Unweighted count`, flow_summary$first_readmitted_n, flow_summary$second_stage_n),
      `NRD-weighted estimate` = c(flow_summary$`NRD-weighted estimate`, flow_summary$first_readmitted_weighted, flow_summary$second_stage_weighted)
    )
    word_flex_table(flow_summary_display, "Cohort totals across annual NRD samples. Weighted values estimate the NRD target universe; pooled values containing suppressed annual cells are shown as Suppressed.",
      c(Stage = 3.5, `Unweighted n` = 1.35, `NRD-weighted estimate` = 1.7), font_size = 8.5)
  } else knitr::kable(flow_summary, caption = "Cohort totals across annual NRD samples. Weighted values are estimates for the NRD target universe; pooled values containing suppressed annual cells are shown as Suppressed.", booktabs = TRUE)
} else {
  cat("Cohort flow output unavailable.")
}
```

The annual counts and weighted totals below are generated from the certified flow outputs. The sequence distinguishes index eligibility, first readmission, and the later survivor risk set; it should not be read as a single unselected HF cohort.

```{r}

}
```

### Primary adjusted association

The crude and adjusted risks share the survivor-conditional analysis population. Crude values are descriptive weighted risks; adjusted values standardize over the selected model covariates.

```{r}
#| label: crude-primary-table

    mutate(
```

### Population characteristics and missingness

```{r}
#| label: table1
if (!is.null(table1)) {
  table1_labels <- label_table1(table1$variable, table1$level)
  format_table1_cell <- function(value, n, scale) {
    if (is.na(value) || is.na(n)) return("Suppressed")
    estimate <- if (scale == "mean") sprintf("%.1f", value) else sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * value)
    sprintf("%s (n = %s)", estimate, scales::comma(n))
  }
  display_t1 <- bind_cols(table1, table1_labels) |>
    mutate(
      Category = ifelse(is.na(summary_scale), "Suppressed", ifelse(summary_scale == "mean", "", Category)),
      `Same hospital` = mapply(format_table1_cell, same_hospital, same_n, summary_scale, USE.NAMES = FALSE),
      `Different hospital` = mapply(format_table1_cell, different_hospital, different_n, summary_scale, USE.NAMES = FALSE),
      `Std. difference` = ifelse(is.na(standardized_difference), "Suppressed", sprintf("%.3f", standardized_difference))
    )
  if (word_output) {
    display_t1 <- display_t1 |>
      filter(!grepl("^index_ynel[0-9]+$", as.character(.data$variable)) | as.character(.data$level) == "1")
  }
  display_t1 <- display_t1 |> select(Variable, Category, `Same hospital`, `Different hospital`, `Std. difference`)
  table1_caption <- "Analytic sample characteristics. Categorical values are unweighted percentages with unweighted n; continuous values are survey-weighted means with unweighted n. APR-DRG severity 0 is no class specified. Legacy Elixhauser flags use the verified ynel1–ynel31 mapping; the Word copy displays the Present row for binary flags, with full detail in the CSV. Cells suppressed under the release rules remain suppressed."
  if (word_output) word_flex_table(display_t1, table1_caption,
    c(Variable = 2.25, Category = 1.0, `Same hospital` = 1.2, `Different hospital` = 1.2, `Std. difference` = 0.9), font_size = 8)
  else knitr::kable(display_t1, caption = table1_caption, booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: missingness-table
if (!is.null(missingness)) {
  safe_sum <- function(x) if (anyNA(x)) NA_real_ else sum(x)
  show_missing <- missingness |>
    group_by(variable, fragmentation_group) |>
    summarise(eligible_n = safe_sum(eligible_n), missing_n = safe_sum(missing_n), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(missing_pct = ifelse(is.na(eligible_n) | is.na(missing_n) | eligible_n <= 0, NA_real_, 100 * missing_n / eligible_n))
  if (word_output) {
    released_nonzero_missing <- show_missing |>
      filter(!is.na(eligible_n), !is.na(missing_n), eligible_n > 0, missing_n > 0) |>
      mutate(
        Variable = unname(variable_labels[as.character(variable)]),
        Group = display_group(fragmentation_group),
        `Eligible n` = scales::comma(eligible_n),
        `Missing n` = scales::comma(missing_n),
        `Missing %` = sprintf("%.1f%%", missing_pct)
      )
    released_nonzero_missing$Variable[is.na(released_nonzero_missing$Variable)] <- released_nonzero_missing$variable[is.na(released_nonzero_missing$Variable)]
    released_nonzero_missing <- released_nonzero_missing |>
      select(Variable, Group, `Eligible n`, `Missing n`, `Missing %`)
    if (nrow(released_nonzero_missing)) {
      word_flex_table(released_nonzero_missing,
        "Released pooled model-variable rows with nonzero missingness. Rows affected by annual suppression are omitted.",
        c(Variable = 2.25, Group = 1.0, `Eligible n` = 1.1, `Missing n` = 1.1, `Missing %` = 1.05), font_size = 8.5)
    } else knitr::asis_output("No released nonzero pooled missingness rows are available.")
  } else {
    released_nonzero_missing <- show_missing |>
      filter(!is.na(eligible_n), !is.na(missing_n), eligible_n > 0, missing_n > 0) |>
      mutate(
        Variable = unname(variable_labels[as.character(variable)]),
        Group = display_group(fragmentation_group),
        `Eligible n` = scales::comma(eligible_n),
        `Missing n` = scales::comma(missing_n),
        `Missing %` = sprintf("%.1f%%", missing_pct)
      )
    released_nonzero_missing$Variable[is.na(released_nonzero_missing$Variable)] <- released_nonzero_missing$variable[is.na(released_nonzero_missing$Variable)]
    released_nonzero_missing <- released_nonzero_missing |>
      select(Variable, Group, `Eligible n`, `Missing n`, `Missing %`)
    if (nrow(released_nonzero_missing)) knitr::kable(released_nonzero_missing,
      caption = "Released pooled model-variable rows with nonzero missingness. Rows affected by annual suppression are omitted.", booktabs = TRUE)
    else knitr::asis_output("No released nonzero pooled missingness rows are available.")
  }
}
```

In the Word table, pooled groups affected by an annual suppression are omitted and are not assumed to be zero. The complete disclosure-reviewed 23-table release, including annual missingness detail, is available through the CSV downloads.

### Sensitivity and secondary analyses

The following estimates are secondary and should not displace the primary adjusted risk difference. Annual rows are descriptive crude weighted estimates; the current analysis did not fit year-specific adjusted effects or subgroup interaction tests.

### Model coefficients and diagnostics

The primary interpretation is based on standardized risks and the absolute risk difference, not individual odds ratios.

```{r}
#| label: coefficient-table
if (primary_available) {
  coefficients_display <- coefficients_primary |> filter(!is.na(.data$term))
  if (word_output) {
    exposure_coefficient <- coefficients_display |> filter(.data$term == "fragmenteddifferent")
    if (nrow(exposure_coefficient)) {
      exposure_display <- tibble::tibble(
        Contrast = "Different versus same hospital",
        `Log-odds coefficient (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(exposure_coefficient$estimate[[1]], exposure_coefficient$ci_low[[1]], exposure_coefficient$ci_high[[1]], "number", 3)
      )
      word_flex_table(exposure_display, "Primary exposure coefficient from the survey-weighted logistic model. This log-odds coefficient is descriptive; standardized risks and the risk difference are the primary effect measures.",
        c(Contrast = 2.2, `Log-odds coefficient (95% CI)` = 4.0), font_size = 8.5)
    }
  } else {
    exposure_coefficient <- coefficients_display |> filter(.data$term == "fragmenteddifferent")
    if (nrow(exposure_coefficient)) safe_kable(exposure_coefficient, "Primary exposure log-odds coefficient. Full released coefficients are in model_coefficients.csv.")
  }
}
if (!is.null(summary_primary) && nrow(summary_primary)) {
  fit_info <- coefficients_primary |> filter(!is.na(.data$term)) |> slice(1)
  if (word_output) {
    dropped <- as.character(summary_primary$dropped_terms[[1]])
    if (is.na(dropped) || !nzchar(dropped)) dropped <- "None"
    diagnostic_display <- tibble::tibble(
      `Model audit field` = c("Analysis model", "Complete-case sample n", "Weighted population estimate", "PSUs / strata", "Survey design degrees of freedom", "Convergence", "Model rank", "Fitted residual degrees of freedom", "Age spline knots (boundary; internal)", "Log index-length-of-stay spline knots (boundary; internal)", "Knot adjustment", "Structurally dropped terms"),
      Value = c(as.character(summary_primary$model[[1]]), format_n(summary_primary$n[[1]]), format_n(summary_primary$weighted_total[[1]]), paste(format_n(summary_primary$psu_n[[1]]), format_n(summary_primary$strata_n[[1]]), sep = " / "), format_n(summary_primary$design_df[[1]]), as.character(fit_info$converged[[1]]), format_n(fit_info$rank[[1]]), format_n(fit_info$df_residual[[1]]), as.character(summary_primary$knots_age[[1]]), format_knot_values(summary_primary$knots_log1p_index_los[[1]]), as.character(summary_primary$knot_adjustment[[1]]), dropped)
    )
    word_flex_table(diagnostic_display, "Primary model population, survey design, fit diagnostics, and outcome-blind spline knots.",
      c(`Model audit field` = 2.9, Value = 3.6), font_size = 9)
  } else {
    summary_display <- summary_primary |>
      select(any_of(c("analysis", "model", "n", "weighted_total", "psu_n", "strata_n", "design_df", "converged", "rank", "knots_age", "knots_log1p_index_los", "knot_adjustment", "dropped_terms", "sample_definition")))
    knitr::kable(summary_display, caption = "Primary model population, survey design, fit diagnostics, and outcome-blind spline knots.", booktabs = TRUE)
  }
  if (!word_output) {
    convergence_text <- if (tolower(as.character(fit_info$converged[[1]])) == "true") "converged" else "did not converge"
    cat("\n\nFor the primary model, logit{Pr(Y = 1 | X)} = β₀ + Xβ. The adjusted risk in each hospital group is the design-based predictive margin averaged over the primary complete-case population; the risk difference is the different-hospital margin minus the same-hospital margin. The coefficient table reports log-odds coefficients and is descriptive of the fitted model, not the primary effect measure. The model ", convergence_text,
        " (rank ", format_n(fit_info$rank[[1]]), "; fitted residual degrees of freedom ", format_n(fit_info$df_residual[[1]]),
        "; survey design degrees of freedom ", format_n(summary_primary$design_df[[1]]), "; ", format_n(summary_primary$psu_n[[1]]),
        " primary sampling units across ", format_n(summary_primary$strata_n[[1]]), " strata).\n\n", sep = "")
    formula_lines <- paste(strwrap(summary_primary$formula[1], width = 94), collapse = "\n")
    cat("Fitted formula from the certified analysis summary:\n\n", formula_lines, "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (word_output) word_flex_table(diagnostic_display, "Primary model population, survey design, fit diagnostics, and outcome-blind spline knots.",
    c(`Model audit field` = 2.9, Value = 3.6), font_size = 8.5)
}
```

The primary model is a survey-weighted logistic regression for the second-readmission outcome. In symbolic form, `logit{Pr(Y = 1 | X)} = β₀ + Xβ`; the exposure coefficient is on the log-odds scale. Adjusted risks are design-based predictive margins over the primary complete-case population, and the risk difference is the different-hospital margin minus the same-hospital margin. The model included hospital-switching exposure, year, sex, payer, ZIP income quartile, county urban–rural category, index-hospital bed size, urban-teaching status and ownership, natural spline terms for age and log(1 + index length of stay), index discharge disposition, APR-DRG severity, and estimable mapped legacy Elixhauser indicators. Full coefficient rows and the exact software formula are available in `model_coefficients.csv` and `analysis_summary.csv`.

\newpage

## Discussion

### Principal findings

```{r}
#| label: principal-finding
#| results: asis
if (primary_available) {
  same <- get_row(risks_primary, "group", "same")
  diff <- get_row(risks_primary, "group", "different")
  rd <- get_risk_difference(contrasts_primary)
  cat("In ", format_n(summary_primary$n[1]), " complete cases, adjusted 30-day risk was ",
      fmt_ci(same$risk, same$ci_low, same$ci_high, "pct", 2), " after a same-hospital first readmission and ",
      fmt_ci(diff$risk, diff$ci_low, diff$ci_high, "pct", 2), " after a different-hospital first readmission. The adjusted risk difference was ",
      fmt_ci(rd$risk_difference, rd$rd_ci_low, rd$rd_ci_high, "pp", 2),
      ". This conditional association applies to people already selected by having a first readmission and surviving to its discharge.", sep = "")
}
```

### Interpretation in context

Hospital switching is a descriptive site-of-care measure. It can represent a necessary transfer, emergency routing, patient preference, access constraints, insurance arrangements, or referral patterns. These data cannot separate those mechanisms or establish that switching itself is detrimental. Comparison with earlier HF fragmentation studies should emphasize differences in exposure, timing, and target population rather than claim that findings are directly contradictory or novel.

### Limitations

Several limitations constrain interpretation. First, the cohort is conditioned on both a first readmission and survival to its discharge. Illness, access, care processes, and other factors may influence entry into this selected group and the subsequent outcome, creating selection bias. Second, administrative claims lack detailed physiologic severity, functional status, patient preference, distance, referral, ambulance routing, hospital capacity, and information exchange. Adjustment for measured baseline characteristics cannot remove residual confounding. Third, the hospital identifier identifies a site, not a care network or continuity of clinicians. Fourth, the diagnosis and transfer definitions are administrative algorithms without local clinical validation; transfer disposition can be imperfect. Fifth, follow-up cannot cross NRD year or state boundaries, and deaths outside the hospital are not observed. Finally, complete-case analyses can be biased if covariate missingness is informative; no missing-category sensitivity analysis was run.

### Conclusions

Among adults with an eligible HF index admission who were readmitted within 30 days and discharged alive from that readmission, a different-hospital first readmission was associated with the subsequent 30-day inpatient admission risk estimated by the revised model. The result is specific to this selected survivor population and does not show that hospital switching causes, prevents, or is itself evidence of fragmented or lower-quality care.

```{r}
#| label: historical-model-comparison
if (!is.null(adjusted_risks) && "model" %in% names(adjusted_risks)) {
  historical_models <- "historical_matched"
  historical_risks <- adjusted_risks |>
    filter(.data$model %in% historical_models) |>
    mutate(
      Model = "Historical matched",
      Group = display_group(group),
      `Adjusted risk (95% CI)` = format_risk_ci(risk, ci_low, ci_high)
    ) |>
    select(Model, Group, `Adjusted risk (95% CI)`)
  if (nrow(historical_risks)) {
    if (word_output) word_flex_table(historical_risks, "The historical specification is refit on the same revised primary complete-case population for a model comparison.",
      c(Model = 2.6, Group = 1.25, `Adjusted risk (95% CI)` = 2.5), font_size = 8)
    else safe_kable(historical_risks, "The historical specification is refit on the same revised primary complete-case population for a model comparison.")
  }

  if (!is.null(adjusted_contrasts) && "model" %in% names(adjusted_contrasts)) {
    historical_differences <- adjusted_contrasts |>
    filter(.data$model %in% historical_models, .data$contrast == "different_vs_same") |>
      mutate(
        Model = "Historical matched",
        `Risk difference (percentage points, 95% CI)` = vapply(seq_len(n()), function(i) fmt_ci(risk_difference[i], rd_ci_low[i], rd_ci_high[i], "pp", 2), character(1))
      ) |>
      select(Model, `Risk difference (percentage points, 95% CI)`)
    if (nrow(historical_differences)) {
      if (word_output) word_flex_table(historical_differences, "This matched historical-specification risk difference is a model comparison, not the revised primary estimate.",
        c(Model = 2.6, `Risk difference (percentage points, 95% CI)` = 3.7), font_size = 8)
      else safe_kable(historical_differences, "This matched historical-specification risk difference is a model comparison, not the revised primary estimate.")
    }
  }
}
```

## Data access and reproducibility

The NRD is a restricted-use data product and person-level data cannot be redistributed. Researchers may obtain annual NRD files through HCUP subject to its data-use requirements. This project releases aggregate tables only after the project’s disclosure review. Raw NRD records, record-level linked cohorts, survey PSU frames, run manifests, private audit ledgers, and credentials are not part of the public release.

The analysis source is maintained separately from the public site. `REPRODUCING.md` documents the aggregate-only public render and the private full rebuild using authorized annual files. This report reads results from the certified aggregate CSV outputs in `results/`; it does not hard-code effect estimates. The current primary run is `20261024T035323+0500` and uses cohort run `20261023T191357+0500`.

The public site provides the full 23-file disclosure-reviewed aggregate contract and the [Word manuscript](index.docx): [cohort flow](../data/cohort_flow.csv), [crude weighted risks](../data/crude_weighted_risks.csv), [adjusted risks (revised-run legacy filename)](../data/adjusted_risks.csv), [adjusted contrasts (revised-run legacy filename)](../data/adjusted_contrasts.csv), [Table 1](../data/table1.csv), [sensitivity results](../data/sensitivity_results.csv), [E-value](../data/e_value.csv), [subgroup results (empty in this run)](../data/subgroup_results.csv), [main-model legacy output](../data/model_main.csv), [conditional-model coefficients](../data/model_conditional.csv), [missingness flow](../data/missingness_flow.csv), [complete-case flow](../data/complete_case_flow.csv), [coarsened transfer exclusions](../data/transfer_exclusions.csv), [first-readmission mortality](../data/first_readmission_mortality.csv), [secondary outcomes](../data/secondary_outcomes.csv), [utilization](../data/utilization.csv), [cost availability](../data/cost_availability.csv), [primary and matched-model risks](../data/model_adjusted_risks.csv), [primary and matched-model contrasts](../data/model_adjusted_contrasts.csv), [model coefficients](../data/model_coefficients.csv), [sensitivity risks](../data/sensitivity_adjusted_risks.csv), [sensitivity contrasts](../data/sensitivity_adjusted_contrasts.csv), and [analysis summary](../data/analysis_summary.csv). The adjusted risks/contrasts and main-model legacy files are revised-run outputs, not historical model estimates. Private manifests, survey frames, record-level data, and audit files are not public.
